newsitem.title: ITALY: Bad weather in Cuba keeps Castro from summit.
newsitem.headline: Bad weather in Cuba keeps Castro from summit.

text.p: Bad weather in Cuba prevented President Fidel Castro from flying to Rome to attend the U.N.-sponsored World Food Summit on Friday, a summit spokeswoman said.

"He's not coming today. He hasn't been able to take off because of weather conditions. This is what we have been told. We hope he will be here tomorrow," Christine Graves of the U.N. Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) said.
Castro had been scheduled to address the summit at around 1300 GMT. His rare trip to Europe was expected to include what would be an historic meeting with Pope John Paul.
"We assume it's the fog. We've been told it was weather conditions," Graves said.

Despite her remarks, confusion continued to surround Castro's travel plans from Havana. Cuba traditionally withholds information on his movements and an embassy official in Rome would make no comment on whether he would come or not.

Italian diplomats said they were still trying to ascertain what Castro's schedule was. The veteran leader, who has been named one of six summit vice-chairmen, had initially been expected to arrive in the early hours of Friday.
